prize_parts.citation: For discoveries in GLP-1 physiology and the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B025 is the one candidate all six of us ranked first, and that agreement rests on substance rather than habit. The arc runs from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect (Holst), through the pleiotropic biology of GLP-1 and its degradation by DPP-4 (Drucker), to degradation-resistant acylated analogues (Knudsen) that lower glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular events. It has been confirmed in large independent randomised outcome trials and over a decade of global use. Few prizes in this field have joined a clear mechanism to a transformation in patient care this directly, and delay now is hard to defend.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Four credited names must be cut to three, the early identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested (Mojsov, and Habener who is not on the list), and Knudsen's contribution is industrial drug design rather than discovery of a mechanism. Any trio leaves out someone with a defensible claim. There is also a framing question about whether we reward physiology, drug development or both, and the answer changes the laureate set.

responses.point: Linnarsson, with El-Manira and Sandberg, proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and leaves Knudsen out to keep the prize on discovery rather than pharmaceutical development.
responses.response: This is a serious argument and I have not dismissed it. I still keep Knudsen, because the Nobel tradition in this category has repeatedly honoured the step that turns a mechanism into a medicine when the mechanism alone did not change practice. Semaglutide and liraglutide only exist because of her acylation strategy. My concern with Mojsov is that her claim rests on peptide identification, and that priority is disputed with Habener, who we cannot name. I would accept the Mojsov variant if the committee settles the priority question, but I would not drop the drug-design step.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks CAR-T (B047) fourth and proposes only June and Sadelain, treating CAR engineering as the core and Rosenberg as a different component.
responses.response: I rank B047 second and keep Rosenberg in the trio, so we differ here. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials supplied the clinical framework in which CARs worked, and a prize restricted to the CAR design alone would understate it. I accept your point that Eshhar's absence is a real gap that no choice among the credited names repairs, and that is why I treat B047 as an alternative and not as my preferred prize.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B038) second as a transformative method for circuit neuroscience, with Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann.
responses.response: I agree about the method's importance, but I place it sixth. It is a research tool, so its medical consequence is indirect and the six-person credit set cannot be resolved in three seats without an acknowledged injustice (Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck are all out). I would not be persuaded to favour it over B025 unless the committee decides that enabling discoveries count the same as direct ones, and even then the allocation problem remains unsolved.

responses.point: Sandberg places splice-switching antisense therapy for SMA (B020) fourth and cGAS-STING (B009) seventh, and stresses how clean the Krainer-Bennett pairing is.
responses.response: I agree the Krainer and Bennett pairing is clean and the clinical effect in infants is dramatic, but I rank it seventh because it is a single-disease success that follows the mechanism by many years, whereas B014 and B047 have broader, population-level effects. On cGAS-STING we agree that the mechanism is excellent but that therapy is not yet validated, so I would not move it ahead of the clinically proven candidates this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third seat in B025, and whether Habener's absence from the credited names distorts the configuration.
Whether the committee reads the prize as rewarding physiology, drug design, or both.
Whether the HPV vaccine (B014) is sufficiently distinct from the 2008 HPV-cancer prize for it to be a serious alternative.
I have not independently verified the priority claims discussed above; they are stated from recollection.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B025. My field is autoimmunity, and B047 and B009 touch on autoimmune disease, but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited person on the shortlist, and I do not infer one from shared institutions or topics.
